title: Security Headers
description: Secure your site and visitors by enforcing essential HTTP security headers.

use_server_config.title: Use server configuration to send headers
use_server_config.description: By default, security headers are sent via PHP. Enable this to inject headers directly into your server configuration (NGINX/Apache).

x_frame_options.title: X-Frame-Options
x_frame_options.description: Prevent your site from being displayed inside another website using frames, helping protect against clickjacking attacks. Learn more.

x_content_type_options.title: X-Content-Type-Options
x_content_type_options.description: Tell browsers not to guess file types, helping block malicious files from being run as something they’re not. Learn more.

referrer_policy.title: Referrer-Policy
referrer_policy.description: Controls how much information about your visitors’ previous pages is shared when they follow links. Learn more.

content_security_policy.title: Content-Security-Policy
content_security_policy.description:
Adds strong protection by limiting which domains browsers can load scripts, styles, and other content from. Learn more.
Use report-uri.com to create your policy, then paste it here.

x_frame_options.ui:warning: Enabling this setting can block your site from being embedded via iframes on other sites — make sure this is what you intend.

x_content_type_options.ui:warning: Ensure your server uses correct MIME types — files or scripts with incorrect types may not work as expected after enabling this setting.

referrer_policy.ui:warning: Stricter policies may limit referrer information shared with other sites — this can affect analytics or integrations that rely on it.

content_security_policy.ui:warning: Be careful when creating your policy — overly strict rules can block scripts, styles, or other content your site needs to function properly.
